H
ail, adventurer! 
Welcome to the 
Western Reaches.
You've found yourself in a 
land of fragile civilizations, 
majestic landscapes, and 
secrets lost to the dark.
This realm of mystery and 
wonder is yours. It is a 
place for bold explorers 
who dare to lift a torch 
high in the face of an 
overwhelming night!
The Western Reaches will 
be shaped by your hands.
Warriors and witches, 
mystics and mages. You 
who are true seekers. 
You who follow a hawk 
across the burning desert, 
who chase a river from 
its humble wellspring to 
its mighty crash into the 
sea, and who watch the 
dawn break from atop the 
mountains.
You will discover who you 
are as you explore this 
realm. Will you become 
the land's protector, its 
conquerer? Will its people 
sing ballads or dirges of 
your deeds?
There's only one way to 
find out, of course.
There are many unknown 
paths that lie before you, 
and there is but one thing 
to do: Find your way.
Within these pages, you'll 
meet your beginnings. 
What you will become is 
being written even now as 
you read these words and 
grasp your destiny.
So light your torch, though 
it is a small flame in the 
dark, and let it be known:
You are here, o fabled land!
-Kelsey Dionne, Feb. 2025

7
WHAT ARE THE 
WESTERN REACHES?
The Western Reaches are a 
place of dangerous fantasy 
adventuring where heroes can 
strike out to explore the land, 
find incredible treasures, and 
make a name for themselves.
This official Shadowdark RPG 
setting combines all the world 
building material from Cursed 
Scroll zines 1-6 (CS 1-6) into a 
regional setting that can be 
traversed from top to bottom.
The Player's Guide to the 
Western Reaches (PGWR) works 
with the Game Master's Guide 
to the Western Reaches (GMWR) 
to outline what players and GMs 
need to know to run and play in 
games in the Reaches.
If you're a player, you'll want to 
avoid the spoilers in the GMWR. 
This book is all you need — it 
will orient you to the Western 
Reaches and help you build a 
character ready to explore them!
HOW DO I PLAY IN 
THIS SETTING?
Check out the Overview chapter 
first (pg. 11) to learn some 
everyday knowledge about the 
Western Reaches.
You as the player will know 
what a typical character in the 
Western Reaches knows about 
the world. That is, not much!
The Reaches are meant to be 
explored and discovered using 
sandbox style gameplay. That 
means the Game Master will 
supply you and your adventuring 
party with rumors, leads, and 
mysteries. But it's up to you to 
decide which threads to pull.
In the Reaches, your fate is in 
your own hands. Will your story 
eventually become a legend? 
The later chapters of this book 
contain character building rules. 
You can also use the official, 
free Shadowdark RPG character 
builder, shadowdarklings.net!

12
What Everyone Knows
Ten things (which may not even 
be true) everyone knows about 
the Western Reaches.
1. The Reaches are ancient. 
They've been here since the sun 
first rose over the western shore. 
Some say the land came up out 
of the sea, or the gods sculpted 
it all out of clay, or the dwarves 
hammered it together on anvils. 
Nobody really knows. But there's 
plenty of old stuff all around that 
must have been built ages ago. 
2. There are faraway lands. 
They say the Reaches stretch all 
the way up to a frozen land of 
endless night, and all the way 
down to deserts so hot they'll 
cook you alive. There's even a big 
city on the coast. City of Masks, 
they call it. Most people don't 
travel too far, though. Too risky. 
3. It's dangerous out there. 
Nobody's going to come riding 
to your rescue! These are lawless 
lands full of bandits and thieves. 
Wild beasts and trolls. Evil spirits. 
You'd better not go alone.
4. The world ends at the Last 
Sea. There's nothing else west 
of the coast. Just the Last Sea 
rolling on and on into mist. 
Some say if you keep going, 
you'll eventually arrive at the 
shores of the gods' realm and 
you can ask them for one thing. 
But you'd never make it back 
from there anyhow. 
5. No king has ever ruled all the 
Reaches. Sure, some have tried. 
But the Reaches have no king, 
not now, not ever. There was 
a queen long ago who almost 
conquered it all from top to 
bottom, but her heart was dark 
and the gods cast her down. 
Every child knows the song: Rise 
and fight, sun from night, dark 
queen tumbles out of sight. 
6. The gods are distant. The 
gods don't walk among us 
anymore. And they don't 
intervene. There are a few 
rare folks like priests who can 
channel their power. That's how 
we know they're still watching 
over us, for good or for ill.

13
7. Ancient spirits and beings 
dwell here. There's all kinds of 
strange demons and ghosts 
lurking around in the wilds. 
You've heard of the Willowman 
who comes to scare children 
who don't listen. He's real! And 
there are other things like him.
8. Magic is terribly dangerous. 
Most folks don't trust a wizard, 
I'll tell you that. Only a madman 
lets a wizard cast a spell in his 
house. You'll get yourself blown 
up that way. Even touching a 
magic sword has half a chance 
of cursing you blind!
9. Non-humans aren't very 
common.  Elves, dwarves, you 
don't often see them. We do 
get a traveler from time to time, 
and the kids always want to ask 
them a barrel of questions. 
10. Most of the Reaches are 
unexplored. You'll hear a couple 
tall tales from sailors, but most 
folks haven't seen much farther 
than the ends of their own 
noses. Hard to believe half the 
stuff those sailors say, anyway. 
None of them have even been to 
the south. Can't sail a boat over 
the desert, can you?

14
Life in the Reaches
POINTS OF LIGHT
The Western Reaches is a "points 
of light" setting where there 
are small pockets of fragile 
civilization, usually in the form of 
self-governed towns and city-
states. Most places outside these 
areas are dangerous and lawless.
MIGHT MAKES RIGHT
When there is no overall rule 
of law, street justice prevails. 
Bandits, monsters, thieves, and 
worse roam the wilds of the 
Western Reaches, often acting 
with impunity against the weak.
Adventurers will have to defend 
themselves, make allies, and act 
wisely if they hope to survive 
outside the safety of civilization. 
The wilds will eventually wear 
down even the toughest 
adventurers. Characters will 
need to retreat back to town on 
a regular basis to rest, restock, 
and recount their exploits in a 
carousing celebration!
ANCESTRIES
Humans are by far the most 
common ancestry in the 
Western Reaches, but there 
are a wide scattering of other 
peoples and civilizations.
Dwarves, elves, and halflings are 
uncommon. Half-orcs, half-elves, 
goblins, and kobolds are rare.

ANCESTRY

15
SOCIAL STRUCTURE
Most people in the Western 
Reaches come from humble 
means and get by working in a 
trade or craft. 
If they live in a city-state or 
its nearby lands, they pledge 
loyalty to its overlord and serve 
as vassals in exchange for the 
overlord's protection.
In most parts of the Reaches, 
there is no overlord. Many towns 
and villages have no other 
authority than their own and 
must protect themselves from 
outside dangers. 
There is no universal set of laws, 
governance, or culture across 
the Western Reaches.
A knight from the Duchy 
of Montmar would not be 
recognized or treated as a noble 
by the lawless bandit lords who 
roam the Djurum Desert. 
A visitor in the City of Masks 
might unknowingly break one 
of the Duke's laws. In Alkesh, 
the very same "crime" might be 
perfectly legal, or perhaps it is 
punished even more harshly.
CIVILIZATIONS
Most people who dwell in the 
Western Reaches have at least 
heard of the other centers of 
power in the region and know a 
few facts about them.
City of Masks. The Duke reigns 
over this romantic city of high 
culture, art, and danger. It's 
the biggest city-state in all the 
Western Reaches. 
Alkesh. A princess called the 
Shar rules Alkesh. The city is 
a mysterious, bright oasis in 
the desert where you can buy 
anything for the right price. 
Stonehall. A dwarf king as old 
as three men presides over a 
vast hall under the mountains. 
The dwarves of Stonehall are the 
best crafters in all the land.
Kyzian Steppes. Wild tribes of 
horseback riders roam across 
the plains like a moving army. 
Their queen is a feared warrior.
Lydonia. An aloof elf king rules 
over a shining citadel deep 
in the forest. His rangers and 
knights watch from behind 
every tree and blade of grass.

Dwarf Ancestry
DWARF
Brave, stalwart folk as sturdy as 
the stone kingdoms they carve 
inside mountains.
You know the Common and 
Dwarvish languages.
Stout. Start with +2 HP. Roll hit 
points per level with advantage.
POPULATION
Dwarves are uncommon and 
reclusive. They account for about 
10% of the population.
ORIGINS
Dwarves are the heartier cousins 
of the fey-like dverg who dwell 
in the Isles of Andrik. Both 
carve out vast, stone halls inside 
mountains. Most dwarves hail 
from their ancestral clans that 
live beneath the Rimespire and 
Bastion mountain chains.

Elf Ancestry
ELF
Ethereal, graceful people who 
revere knowledge and beauty. 
Elves see far and live long.
You know the Common, Elvish, 
and Sylvan languages.
Farsight. You get a +1 bonus 
to attack rolls with ranged 
weapons or a +1 bonus to 
spellcasting checks.
POPULATION
Elves are uncommon but widely 
known in the Reaches. They 
form 10% of the population.
ORIGINS
Many free-spirited elves roam 
the Djurum Desert in nomadic 
tribes that flow with the seasons 
and winds. Others live in the 
quiet stillness of the Sablewood, 
kept safe by the rangers and 
knights who serve the King of 
the Wood in his citadel, Lydonia.

Goblin Ancestry
GOBLIN
Green, clever beings who thrive 
in dark, cramped places. As 
fierce as they are tiny.
You know the Common and 
Goblin languages.
Keen Senses. You can't be 
surprised (you roll initiative 
during surprise rounds and are 
not treated as unaware).
POPULATION
Goblins are very rare, comprising 
only 5% of the population.
ORIGINS
Goblins come mainly from the 
deepest parts of the Sablewood 
and in the cave systems beneath 
the Rimespire Mountains. 
They are very environmentally 
adaptable, and it's thought 
that large tribes of goblins live 
in remote areas that have little 
contact with the outside world.

Half-Elf Ancestry
HALF-ELF
Lithe, long-lived humans with 
subtle elven features. Their 
boldness is tempered by insight.
You know the Common and 
Elvish languages, plus one 
additional common language.
Adaptable. Roll your talent rolls 
twice and choose which result to 
keep.
POPULATION
Half-elves are rarely seen. They 
make up 5% of the population.
ORIGINS
Half-elves typically hail from the 
Kyzian Steppes or the Djurum 
Desert where their parents 
have the greatest crossover in 
territory. They are beloved by 
both peoples and seen as a 
symbol of alliance. Half-elves 
often become legendary horse 
riders, archers, and leaders.

Half-Orc Ancestry
HALF-ORC
Towering, tusked warriors who 
are as daring as humans and as 
relentless as orcs. 
You know the Common and 
Orcish languages.
Mighty. You have a +1 bonus to 
attack and damage rolls with 
melee weapons.
POPULATION
Half-orcs are quite rare, making 
up only 5% of the population.
ORIGINS
Barbarian tribes of orcs rove 
north of the Gilzai Mountains 
and into the Kyzian Steppes, 
where they sometimes cross 
paths with human tribes. Some 
of these groups share a mutual 
worship of the warrior god 
Ramlaat, and half-orcs can result 
from this rare cultural merging.

HALFLING
Small, cheerful country folk with 
mischievous streaks. They enjoy 
life’s simple pleasures.
You know the Common

OVERVIEW
Factions are organizations the 
PCs can join that have specific 
missions and bylaws.
PCs who join a faction have the 
opportunity to accrue special 
benefits as long as they remain 
in good standing.
Parties who have multiple PCs 
from the same faction will 
accrue benefits more quickly.
LEADERSHIP
Each faction has an NPC leader 
who holds final authority over 
the faction's members, bylaws, 
and proceedings. 
The faction leader can decide 
the outcome of any disputes 
between members or leave the 
decision up to a majority vote.
A new leader must make a DC 
15 CHA check for a peaceful 
transfer of power. On a failure, 
the faction splinters into 2 
conflicting organizations. 
BEING IN A FACTION
Joining. PCs can join a faction 
by participating in an initiation 
ceremony. A PC can only be in 
one faction at a time and must 
renounce prior factions in order 
to change to a new one.
Standing. PCs remain in good 
standing with a faction as long 
as they follow its bylaws. PCs 
caught breaking the bylaws can 
be expelled from the faction by 
a majority vote of its members or 
by the faction's leader.
PCs who leave a faction lose 
access to its benefits.
Benefits. Combine the levels of 
all PCs in the party who are in 
the same faction to determine 
which faction benefits they gain. 
Only members of the faction 
gain its benefits. 
If a PC leaves the party due to 
any reason other than death, 
subtract their LV from their 
faction's total. This may cause 
the party to lose benefits.

are not accustomed to enduring,

NEW WARBANDS
Create a new warband using the 
following guidelines:
1. Start with a creature of LV 1-5 
that could form a combat unit.
2. Double its level.
3. It has (8 x LV) + CON mod HP.

A warband is a group of up to 20 
similar combatants. Treat it as a 
single creature. A warband that 
falls to 0 HP is destroyed.  
Attacks. A warband's attacks 
fill a near-sized area around 
its target. It can disperse its 
damage dice between anything

Unique Beings. PCs and level 6+

morale checks. It checks morale 
when it falls to half HP and each 
time it takes damage while 
below half HP. On a failure, it 
has a 3:6 chance of a rout (being 
destroyed while fleeing). 
Leadership. If you join one of 
your warbands, it has ADV on 
morale checks. You move with it 
but act independently. 
MAINTAINING
Cost. A warband costs 10 gp x 
its level each month to feed and 
maintain. If you are in arrears, 
the warband makes a morale 
check each week. Upon a failure, 
the warband deserts.
Healing. Warbands heal 1d4 HP 
per day unless otherwise noted.
Retraining. You can change the 
upgrades your warbands have. 
Doing so takes 1 week.
